decisions.statement: A file to write is named at `--file-path`.
The body for that file is read from the file `--content-file` names.
A `--file-path` that no `--content-file` closes is given the body piped in.
A second `--file-path` opening before the first is closed is refused.
A `--content-file` following no `--file-path` is refused.
A path named at `--remove` is left with no body at all.
A path `--remove` names that no commit and no working tree holds is refused.
A file beside a path taken away is taken away with that path.
A path named more than once by one call is refused.
A path both written and taken away by one call is refused.
A path outside the repository is refused.
A path the repository bars is refused.
A body piped in that opens a line with the payload marker is refused.
A body that is not text refuses the call rather than being carried on.
A call naming no file to write and no path to take away is refused.
A flag this takes no spelling of is refused naming the call and what it takes.
A caller names which flags take a value, and the flags here answer where none does.
A caller names which flags carry no value, and `--restated` answers where none does.
The readings the writer owes are answered as faults of the call.
The change kind read here is the kind of the change the caller runs.
A commit message is read from the command line or worked out from the paths.
`--restated` names the change kind a restatement lands under.
A change kind no page here declares refuses the call.
Nothing here lands or commits.
Nothing here judges a body.

definition: the files a command line names, and the body each file is left with
